elements.problem: The orthostatic decision is 'systolic drop >= 20 OR diastolic drop >= 10'. The rules encode only systolic >= 20 (and systolic < 20 for the No branch). Diastolic drop is never measured or evaluated, so patients with a diastolic-only drop miss orthostatic hypotension and can wrongly fall into hyperventilation or common faint. Hb thresholds are not_representable; ECG-abnormal-refer and substance-use/BP cross-references are management/cross-reference.

summary: The most consequential problem is the orthostatic hypotension decision: the page says systolic drop >= 20 or diastolic drop >= 10, but the rules only test systolic, which also corrupts the hyperventilation and common faint branches. The red box itself is well encoded (all danger signs present with correct and/or logic), with minor losses (asymmetric, allergen recency, 'following vaccination') and the footnote 'shock likely' criteria missing. Measure tasks do not collect the SBP, pulse or glucose that the priority rule uses. SNOMED concept choices were judged by name only; I did not verify the existence of every concept.
